cohort: The study included 47 mothers giving birth to macrosomic babies (>=4000 gm) and 47 mothers giving birth to normal birth weight babies (2500-3999 gm).
finding: Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and weight gain during pregnancy were strong independent risk factors for macrosomia, which was also associated with a higher incidence of diabetes in pregnancy, CS-related morbidity, and neonatal hypoglycemia.
mod_finding: The incidence of morbidity related to Caesarean Sections was high among mothers giving birth to macrosomic babies.
birth_weight: Macrosomic babies >=4000 gm; control babies 2500-3999 gm.
